Confirmed and rendered. Summary of what I checked and changed:

**Audit result**: nearly every mention of "Column Width" / "Column width" in the article's prose (intro, all 5 steps' body text, and both notes in step 3) was **already bolded**. The only place it wasn't was the **H1 title** — `Column Width — Adjust the Width of Menu Items`.

**Change made**: bolded the phrase in `job.title` → `**Column Width** — Adjust the Width of Menu Items`, then re-ran `snap_render_job` to regenerate `column-width-adjust-menu-items.md`. Verified via `snap_job` read that the title persisted correctly. No step images changed content (title-only edit), so there was nothing new to `snap_view`.

**One thing I deliberately did NOT change**, and want to flag rather than silently decide: step headings "Find Column width in the item editor" and "Set a fixed column width" still contain the phrase unbolded. In this job format the step `heading` string is reused verbatim as both the `## N. heading` line *and* the image's `alt` text (`![heading](img)`). Adding `**` there would render fine in the heading but would leak literal asterisk characters into the alt attribute (visible to screen readers / on broken image load) — a real defect, not a style choice. If you do want those two headings bolded too, let me know and I'll take that trade-off (or you can rename the headings to avoid the phrase and add a bolded mention in the adjoining body sentence instead, which is already the case for both steps).
